A.explanation: This is a couple of two $30\text{ N}$ forces $2.0\text{ m}$ apart, so torque is $30 \times 2.0 = 60\text{ N m}$, not $30\text{ N m}$.

B.explanation: The $40\text{ N}$ and $10\text{ N}$ forces are not equal and act in the same direction, so they do not form a couple.

C.explanation: The $25\text{ N}$ and $5\text{ N}$ forces are not equal in magnitude, so they do not form a couple.

D.explanation: This is a couple of two equal opposite $15\text{ N}$ forces $2.0\text{ m}$ apart, so torque is $15 \times 2.0 = 30\text{ N m}$.

hints: Notice the two requirements for a couple: the two forces must be equal in size and opposite in direction, with a perpendicular separation between them.
Recall torque of a couple is one force multiplied by the perpendicular distance between the lines of action: $torque = F \times d$.
Check each diagram for equal opposite forces, then multiply that force by the $1.0\text{ m}$ or $2.0\text{ m}$ separation to see which gives $30\text{ N m}$.
walkthrough: Identify a couple: two forces equal in magnitude, parallel but opposite in direction, separated by a perpendicular distance.
State the rule: torque of couple $= F \times d$, where $F$ is one of the forces and $d$ is the perpendicular separation.

Option A gives $30\text{ N} \times 2.0\text{ m} = 60\text{ N m}$. Options B and C are not couples because the two magnitudes $40\text{ N}$ with $10\text{ N}$ and $25\text{ N}$ with $5\text{ N}$ are unequal.
Option D has two $15\text{ N}$ forces in opposite directions with $d = 2.0\text{ m}$.
Calculate: $15 \times 2.0 = 30$, with units $\text{N m}$. This matches the required $30\text{ N m}$. This is option D.
